correctness.rationale: The Plücker form is split of dimension six, with its zero locus consisting of zero and the rank-two (decomposable) alternating tensors. A nondegenerate orthogonal splitting exists because the two-dimensional kernel is anisotropic over an odd field. The signed discriminants multiply for this even-dimensional splitting: the split six-space has square signed discriminant, the anisotropic plane has nonsquare signed discriminant, so the complement is a minus-type four-space. Via β it defines a form on W that changes only by scalar when the volume form changes. The fiber t has orthogonal lift x and all lifts x+u; the equation is Q(u)=−Qβ(t). The anisotropic norm plane represents zero once and every nonzero scalar q+1 times. For t≠0 every isotropic lift is nonzero, and each wedge factorization set is an SL₂(F_q) torsor. For t=0, the q⁴ pairs with first vector zero and q(q⁴−1) remaining dependent pairs give q⁵+q⁴−q. In H⊥A, the zero count is (2q−1)+(q²−1)(q−1), proving both target multiplicities. The displayed nonsquare construction really is anisotropic and its perpendicular lift has f=−a, e=−δb, giving the stated target formula. Bilinearity gives the group law, the k-th power is (kv,kz), and commuting with every quotient vector forces v=0. Surjectivity of the word map on W gives the derived group W; two free central coordinates multiply each fiber by q⁸. Independent full quotient-pair and lift enumeration for q=3 and 5 matched every target and all multiplicities.
residual_risks: The finite checks use one representative over each of two prime fields. They do not independently sample extension fields or arbitrary kernels; the norm and orthogonal-splitting proof is the uniform argument.

evidence: Gow–Quinlan provide the decomposable-free kernel background. Levit–Shwartz give isotropic tuple counts and a full-contraction-rank case, whose rank hypothesis is not met here (each nonzero contraction has rank 3 into dimension 4).

Naik's Theorem 1.3 realizes any prescribed number of different nonidentity fiber sizes in a class-two family by other quotients. For two sizes his §3 construction is a one-dimensional kernel in the six-dimensional exterior square, not a two-dimensional kernel. Kaushik–Yadav Theorem A directly implies that all central targets occur for the prime-field groups here, since the only noncentral conjugacy-class size is p³, but it classifies support rather than sizes.
broader_coverage.reasoning: There is broader prior coverage of qualitative nonuniformity and of prime-field surjectivity. Neither determines which specified nonzero targets have small versus large fibers, or the sizes and multiplicities for this family.

evidence: Lemma 2.4 determines the identity fiber from the conjugacy data and reduces other sizes to counts of quotient elements whose contraction image contains the target. The coset-sum method in §3 still requires sizes of K(G) intersected with separate cosets. Theorem A only gives membership in the support. In the frozen proof the quotient splitting identifies those intersections as fibers of an anisotropic norm at −Qβ(t), and locates the small-fiber locus in the canonical minus-type cone.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The remaining calculation is not a change of normalization or a substitution into the inspected conjugate-type formulas. Those leave an undetermined target-specific incidence number; the orthogonal projection evaluates and organizes it for the exact family. The underlying facts about finite-field quadrics and the coset-sum principle are standard.

originality.rationale: The distinct finding is the per-target spectrum and exact elliptic-null-cone stratification for the anisotropic two-dimensional kernel, uniformly over odd prime powers. The existence and maximal kernel dimension, general coset-summing method for commutator fibers, occurrence of multiple nonzero fiber sizes in some constant-conjugate-type groups, and (for prime q) the support being all of G′ already have prior coverage. They are not credited as original here.
residual_risks: A bounded comparison does not establish historical priority. An equivalent table under older quadric projection, word measure, or rank distribution terminology may exist. Classical plane-section counts and group classification themselves are not credited as novel.

value.rationale: The extremal four-dimensional quotient retaining dependence as the zero-commutator criterion is a natural test of how much conjugacy data control word measures. Constant contraction rank gives a single noncentral conjugacy size but not a single size of nonidentity word fibers. Supplying the exact canonical target locus, two sizes, and their populations for the whole odd-field family gives information a user of the word distribution cannot read from a group census, the identity fiber, or the support classification. This is more than producing a single instance of a previously known nonuniformity phenomenon.
residual_risks: The value is the exact family-specific spectrum; it does not require or establish a classification of all class-two groups of this order or a result in characteristic two.
